lesson: The accrual ratio is a WEAK kill criterion for payables-funded working-capital frauds: PC Jeweller's accrual ratio held at 0.02 while cumulative CFO/PAT broke to 0.34, because the inventory build is financed through trade payables (gold metal loans), which never passes through the accrual line.
evidence: prediction 2017-12-31-cccdf1de45b8:accrual_ratio_latest HELD
prediction 2017-12-31-cccdf1de45b8:cum_cfo_pat BROKEN actual=0.3439
action: Kill-criteria selection should weight cash-conversion and stock-flow criteria over accrual criteria when the funding channel is payables-side; consider a payables-divergence criterion (payables growth vs COGS growth) for this model.

lesson: Broadcasting the report's single confidence (0.38) as P(holds) for every criterion is miscalibrated by construction: the two cash criteria deserved a lower P(holds) than the accrual criterion on the report's own reasoning. Brier 0.224 barely beats a coin flip despite the verdict being right.
evidence: brier_by_agent core.report.criteria = 0.2244
action: criteria.py should assign per-criterion probabilities (e.g. flagged-check criteria get P(holds) well below 0.5; clean-check criteria above), not one broadcast confidence. A calibration question for the golden set.

lesson: Comparative-column restatements of the CASH FLOW statement are themselves a forensic signal: the FY18 filing restated FY17 CFO from 756.48 to 794.35 (+37.87cr, +5%) and its restated FY17 CFS legs do not tie to the printed net change (794.35-530.06-47.45 != 311.74) - the V7 identity refuses the column. A company revising its cash history upward while its current cash collapses is quiet-change material (pattern P5).
evidence: AR-FY17-PCJ-AR-FY17.pdf cashflow FY17 = 756.48
AR-FY18-PCJ-AR-FY18.pdf comparative FY17 = 794.35 (registered, classified 'restated' by quarantine)
action: A deterministic restatement-log across filings (metric, period, old, new, delta) is nearly free from the quarantine's 'restated' classifications and should reach the report as its own section.

lesson: A treasury-heavy company systematically shows CFO/PAT below 1.0 without any earnings-quality problem: the indirect-method cash flow subtracts interest and dividend income from PBT in operating activities and reports it under investing. Symphony earns ~20% of PBT as treasury income on a ~Rs 422cr investment book and converts 0.55; the check reads that as a HIGH flag.
evidence: other_income_share FY18 = 0.2044
cfo_pat_latest FY18 = 0.5550
non-current + current investments FY18 = 17,200.65 + 25,035.83 lacs
action: Do NOT move the cfo_pat threshold on one observation. The golden set should test whether cfo_pat needs an other-income adjustment (CFO vs PAT-excluding-investment-income) or whether other_income_share should modulate the flag's severity. Recorded as a calibration question, not a code change (ADR-0048).

lesson: Choosing a company to test FALSE POSITIVES found three defects in one run, where two fraud runs found none of them. A clean company with unusual-but-legitimate structure (stub period, outsourced manufacturing, treasury book) exercises paths a fraud never touches.
evidence: ADR-0048 defects 1-3, all first observed on Symphony
action: Keep alternating: the golden set should be built as matched pairs (a fraud and a clean company of the SAME business shape), not as a list of frauds.

source: first lender filing read end-to-end (FY25, ADR-0050)
lesson: A capability can be fully unit-tested, calibrated on real figures, documented as validated, selected by config — and still be unreachable from a real document. The lender path was broken in three independent places (vocabulary, shape detection, check evaluation) while quality.py's lender functions passed every test they had.
evidence: 7 lender checks with no evaluator in checks.py
statement_shape never set loan_book_to_assets
VALIDATION_TIER0.md cited as proof the firm handles lenders
action: For any claimed capability, ask what a REAL DOCUMENT would have to travel through to exercise it, and test that path — not the leaf function. Candidate audit: which other checks in the playbooks have no evaluator? (contract_asset_divergent, guarantees_heavy, capitalised_cost_heavy, adjusted_ebitda_gap, revenue_inflation partially.)

lesson: A lender needs an earnings-quality measure to replace CFO/PAT, which is now suppressed because it tracks book growth. Candidates: accrual-style measures on net interest income vs credit cost, or the gap between reported PAT and (NII - opex - credit cost). Not invented here — a golden-set calibration question.
evidence: CreditAccess CFO/PAT +2.12 (book -3.3%) vs -3.27 (book grew)
action: Add to the golden-set design: a lender pair (a clean grower and a known lender fraud) is needed to calibrate any replacement measure, since the failure mode is precisely a growing book.

source: ADR-0052 — asset-quality checks running on real note data
lesson: The verdict ladder reads FLAGS but not the PATTERN of flags. CreditAccess fires gnpa_drift (HIGH, Stage-3 1.18%->4.79%) and escalates to FORENSIC_CAUTION, while every corroborating check says honest recognition: reserve_suppression PASSES because the credit-cost rate was RAISED 1.80%->7.95%, and provision coverage is 107% of the impaired book. ADR-0012 encoded exactly this distinction and the screen respects it; the ladder collapses it.
evidence: gnpa_drift FLAG +3.61pp
reserve_suppression PASS (raised)
provision_coverage_low PASS at 107%
VALIDATION_TIER0 concluded REVIEW on the same company
action: Golden set: does a HIGH flag deserve FORENSIC_CAUTION when the exculpatory checks in its own family all pass? Candidate rule — escalation requires either a SEVERE flag, two HIGH flags, or a HIGH flag WITHOUT a passing counter-check in the same family. Do NOT change caution_min_severity on one observation.

lesson: Reading a note is cheap once statements are read, because the note's own reconciliation to the face is a stronger verifier than anything in the note's typography — and it doubles as proof of basis (standalone vs consolidated), which a note heading never states.
evidence: a note claiming gross-as-net passed every page-level check and was caught only by the face tie
action: Apply the same pattern to contingent liabilities (guarantees_heavy), segment revenue (unit_economics), and related-party totals — each reconciles to a face line or to a disclosed total.

source: cash-yield series FY19-FY26 measured across all 12 readable company-years (ADR-0059)
lesson: A series across one company's years is a sharper calibration instrument than a labelled case, and it needs no label. Reading cash_interest_inconsistent for ONE year (FY23) framed CAL-1 as a threshold question; reading all eight years of the same company showed the check fires only where the balance moved violently, which is an estimator defect. The failing case could not have said that on its own.
evidence: balance moved +525/+60/+291/-50/-71/+72/+550/-1% in the same years
PCJEWELLER (the set's positive) 5.34/5.38/4.23% - never near the 2.60% floor
action: Before treating any check's outcome as a calibration question, plot it across every company-year the firm can read. Add series-sweep as a standing step in the golden-set method (GOLDEN_SET.md), alongside labelled cases.

lesson: A point estimate presented to a threshold is a claim about precision. Every flow-over-average-stock rate in the library (cash yield, cost of debt, accrual ratio) divides a year of flow by the mean of two balance-sheet endpoints and then compares it to a floor as though it were measured; on Alkyl FY23 the same two endpoints support 1.64% and 5.64% equally, and the 2.55% mean produced a SEVERE flag on a clean company.
evidence: ALKYLAMINE FY23 cash+bank 62.57 -> 18.23cr, interest 1.03cr
check fired once in 12 company-years, on the clean company
cost of debt band on the same run: 3.9%-14.6% against a 10% ceiling
action: Look for the same shape wherever else a computed number meets a threshold without carrying how well it is known: window CAGRs read off two endpoint years, and ratios with a near-zero denominator (PCJ other_income_share read 695.5% of a collapsed PBT).

lesson: The 'never charge a company for our own missing extractor' rule has to be enforced at every layer that can publish, not once. ADR-0051 fixed it for UNAVAILABLE checks; the disclosure_gap check reproduced it one layer up by folding unreadable rows into the mandated-absent list, and flagged Alkyl Amines MEDIUM over a Total Assets row our locator missed and had already recovered from the balancing line.
evidence: ALKYLAMINE FY23 disclosure_gap FLAG detail named balance_sheet:Total Assets 49,881.61 vs 1,59,008.74 at p.86 l.55
action: When adding any new field that reaches a verdict, ask who the gap belongs to and give the answer a type, not a comment. CheckRecord.gap did this for checks; ExternalInputs now does it for rows.

lesson: A pattern echo is not a reading. The scan charged Five-Star with not printing three mandated tables it prints on the page — 'CWIP aging schedule' (American spelling), 'Trade payables (Ageing Schedule)' (a parenthesis), 'Debt/Equity Ratio' (a slash) — and the first grep to check the charge drowned the disclosed table under case-insensitive hits of 'Managing'. The charge fell only when the CWIP note itself was read.
evidence: FIVESTAR-AR-FY26.pdf p.182 'CWIP aging schedule'
p.192 'Trade payables (Ageing Schedule)'
MDA 'Debt/Equity Ratio3 Times 1.11 1.26'
action: Before publishing any 'not disclosed' claim, read the note that would contain it; and any scanner whose absence-claim feeds a verdict must match on canonicalised text (scan_schedule_iii now does).

source: ADR-0060 — the division-scoping theory the control killed
lesson: The first theory for the missing ageing tables — Schedule III Division III exempts NBFCs — was plausible, unfalsifiable from the failing company alone, and wrong. The other Division III filer in bronze (CreditAccess) prints all three tables findably, which killed the theory in one grep and redirected the diagnosis to orthography.
evidence: CREDITACC-AR-FY26.pdf p.105 'Trade Payables ageing schedule', p.74 'Current ratio 1.38 1.56'
action: When a mandate theory would exempt a company from a charge, test it against a peer filer of the same division before adopting it. One control company is cheap and decisive.

lesson: A check that prints 'coverage' while computing whole-book allowance / Stage-3 gross is publishing a number laxer than its name: it has never read below 55% on any lender-year and reads 121% on CreditAccess, while the stage-3 PCR the term means reads 41.4% on Five-Star. The golden case passed its must_not_flag for this definitional reason, not for its pre-registered collateral rationale — a case passing for the wrong reason is a finding, not a pass.
evidence: sweep: whole-book 119/91/55/107/121% vs stage-3 PCR 54.3/51.3/41.4% (FIVESTAR) across readable lender-years
CREDITACC Reg 52(4) states PCR 65.4% where the check printed 121%
action: The words a deterministic check publishes are part of its contract: name the measure computed. The floor itself is CAL-2 — untouched until a lender positive exists to calibrate against.

lesson: Every enumeration failure this session was SILENT: a subcategory filter with the wrong parent category returns zero rows (not an error), a 'corrected' double space in the exchange's own string would match nothing forever, a throttled API returns partial pages with HTTP 200, and a window that starts after a regime began makes a late event look like the first. None of these can be caught downstream; each needs its own control at the enumeration layer.
evidence: strCat=-1 + subcategory returned 0 rows where the paired category returned 50
39-window sweep saw 3 of October 2021's 10 Gayatri default disclosures; the window alone returned 10, three times
SEBI default-disclosure regime began 2020-01-01 — no register can see a 2019 default
action: Two-pass union for enumeration; verbatim vocabulary with the typography preserved; regime start dates recorded in case labels; never treat an empty API answer as 'none' without a control that proves the query CAN return rows.

lesson: A cold run on an unfamiliar company is the cheapest honest audit of the whole stack: one run measured the walker (missed a filing's balance sheet entirely, read another's faithfully), the check library (REVIEW reached off rows carrying little of the real signal), the case instrument (extraction assertions caught 5 absences and 1 cross-filing restatement), and the docs (the FY17/FY18 ARs disagree by Rs 95.7cr on the same figure). Hand-fixing quirks before the first run would have hidden all of it.
evidence: GAYATRI-FY18 first eval: screen REVIEW in band, 5/6 verified facts unreproduced
FY17 receivables: FY17 AR face 85,036.43 lakh vs FY18 AR comparative 75,464.88 lakh
action: For every new company: pre-register the case BEFORE the first pipeline run, and treat the first run as the diagnostic, never as the deliverable.

lesson: The EPC siphon geometry lives in rows no universal check reads: advances to sub-contractors for works that never commenced (Rs 713.81cr, auditor EoM 'long pending for recovery'), claims receivable up 3x, deposits with contractees, loans to subsidiaries/associates — all grouped under 'Other Current Assets', which the universal library treats as one opaque number. Receivables/revenue divergence read only +12.5pp because the working capital hid one level deeper.
evidence: GAYATRI FY18 note 11: other current assets Rs 1,299.85cr of which advances to sub-contractors Rs 713.81cr
auditor Emphasis of Matter p.56
action: When the EPC playbook is wired (CAP-EPC), its inputs are note-level: the other-current-assets composition, not the face row. Same lesson as the lender path (ADR-0052): the face of the statements is not where model-specific fraud lives.
